correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the structural proof from the assigned RESULT.md. Calderón–Walton H(Q)~k Qhat identifies the quiver whose vertices are ordered pairs and arrows synchronous pairs. Acyclicity of Q implies Qhat acyclic. Its path algebra has Dynkin finite, extended Dynkin tame, wild otherwise (Gabriel/Donovan-Freislich/Nazarova). Every vertex v contributes diagonal degree (deg^- v)^2+(deg^+ v)^2: parallel arrows yield a >=4-arrow Kronecker subquiver; branching >=3 or mixed (2,1) yields star >4 leaves, spectral radius >2. Exactly (2,0)/(0,2) creates an affine D4~ four-star; any further original connected arrow adds a diagonal edge, strictly enlarging a connected affine graph and forcing spectral radius >2. Thus nonwild components are directed paths or isolated 3-vertex forks. Ordered fork squares: same orientation one D4~, opposite orientation one A3~, remainder isolated; mixed fork/path yield A paths. For directed paths each indecomposable is an interval, counted by synchronous length-l path pairs, matching dim. Independently checked finite DAG/Cartan eigenvalues for 572 cases and explicit fork products, not an infinite substitute.

value.rationale: Finite/tame/wild representation type is a canonical central invariant of finite-dimensional face algebras; the result supplies an exact original-quiver recognition criterion, multiplicities of affine factors and a natural finite-type indecomposable-count invariant, all useful without recomputing a potentially large squared quiver.

final_claim: For a finite acyclic quiver Q over algebraically closed k, its Hayashi face algebra is finite-type iff every component of Q is a coherently directed path; tame-infinite iff components are directed paths or exactly the two orientations of a 3-vertex fork and at least one fork; wild otherwise. If f+ and f- count the two fork orientations, the square has f+^2+f-^2 affine D4~ factors and 2f+f- affine A3~ factors. In finite type the # indecomposable modules equals dim algebra=sum_l(sum_i max(n_i-l,0))^2.
